_about: The Forgotten Chapel and its archive.
alden: There are no prayers left for what approaches tonight.
Then perhaps we need answers instead.
Answers have a habit of arriving after they're useful.
You're Orin's apprentice. The one who left.

choice.text: I'm the one who came back.
Orin's missing. I'm looking for him.

alden.text: Mara gave me this. The bell's tuning pin. It's marked with thirteen tolls.
Thirteen. ...Yes. I have seen that number written down. Once. Before it was sealed away.

alden: Our oldest records are behind that door. The archive. I have tried to open it for twenty years.
Three seals: flame, moon and crown. Press them in the right order and it opens. Press them wrongly and...
...nothing happens, actually. Which is somehow worse.
There is an inscription beside the door. My eyes are too old to read what is left of it.

alden.text: Perhaps younger ears will hear more than my eyes can see. Orin always said this place listens back.

alden: The inscription by the archive door. Read what you can. Listen for the rest.
Before the crown, the fire. Before the fire, the moon. Old riddles always run backwards. Like memory.
Read it backwards, Rowan. What came first? The moon, watching alone. Then the fire. Then, last of all, the crown.
Twenty years. And you open it in an evening. I should feel insulted. Mostly I feel afraid.
Go on. Whatever is in there has waited long enough.
I will start a new record tonight. One that no bell can take. Written by everyone, so it would have to be forgotten by everyone.

alden.text: Those marks in the margin. I have heard the child, Pip, humming something with that shape. Ask Pip.

alden: A song for everyone to sing at once. Of course. You cannot steal from a whole village at the same moment.
...Or perhaps you can. But it is harder. And harder is not nothing.
chapel_inscription: Words carved into the stone beside the archive door. Most have been worn smooth.
“...the crown... fire was born... moon watched...”

chapel_inscription.text: Worn away. But stone remembers longer than people do. (Stand close and press F to listen.)
If I listen, maybe the rest comes back.

chapel_inscription: “Before the crown, the fire was born. Before the fire, the moon watched alone.”
chapel_inscription_echo: The worn letters fill with pale light, one line at a time.
“Before the crown, the fire was born. Before the fire, the moon watched alone.”
A riddle about what came first.
chapel_archive_door: A heavy stone door set into the wall. Beside it, three seals: a flame, a moon and a crown.
No handle. No keyhole. Just the seals.
chapel_seal_solved: The archive door swings inward. Cold, dry air spills out, smelling of old paper.
It's open. After twenty years... Go, Rowan. I'll follow.
chapel_ledger: A heavy book on the lectern, bound in cracked leather. A bell is pressed into the cover.
So that is why the records have holes.

choice.text: Then we can take that permission away.

chapel_ledger: No. Not knew. But I have always felt like a man who hid something, and then lost the key.
Then we can take that permission away.
There's something in the spine of the ledger...

args: Found: an iron key stamped with a bell

chapel_ledger: The north gate. The tower road. Orin hid his key where only someone who read all of this would ever find it.
Go. I'll stay with the book. Someone should remember it, now that it has been read.
I should read all of it. Whatever's in here, Orin wanted it found.
chapel_ledger_echo: A figure kneels beside the lectern, hands pressed flat on the open book. Grey robe. Bent back.
[wave amp=10 freq=2]Forgive me. I thought I could choose which memories it would take.[/wave]

chapel_ledger_echo.text: That voice. I... I was there. I held the lamp while he cut the pages out. I asked him why, and he said: so they cannot choose to forget it again.
And then the bell rang, and I forgot I had ever asked.

chapel_chorus_echo: For a heartbeat the pews are full. Villagers stand shoulder to shoulder in their old clothes, mouths open...
...singing. All of them at once. You can't hear the tune, only the feeling of it: many voices holding one thing up.
That wasn't a hymn. That was something older.
chapel_shelves: Parish records, recipe books, and a treatise titled ON THE PROPER STORAGE OF TURNIPS, VOLUME III.
Every record from before the bell was cast is missing. Not burned. Cut out, neatly.
chapel_altar: The altar cloth is embroidered with a golden bell. Someone has stitched over the clapper, again and again, until it's a knot.
chapel_statue: A statue of a robed figure holding a small bell. Its head lies on the floor beside it.
Someone has placed a candle by the head, very respectfully. Someone else has drawn a moustache on it.
chapel_donations: The donation box contains one button, a dried bean, and an IOU signed PIP.
chapel_window: Stained glass: villagers in a ring, mouths open, beneath a rising moon. There is no bell anywhere in the picture.

chapel_window.text: They're singing. Of course they are.

chapel_archive_shelf: Ledgers of births, marriages and harvests. Every few pages, a name has been scraped out of the paper.
